results.reason: Issue 5 says § 2.2 automatically renews for successive five-year terms. It cites the 270/240-day notice window as a narrow 30-day band and says missing it locks Harrowgate in through 2032.

Issue 1 identifies § 3.1 as covering all glass and PET containers for any beverage, worldwide. It contrasts this with the term sheet's amber beer bottles at U.S./Canadian facilities. Issues 1 and 8 confirm Harrowgate is bound by the executed text.
Issue 3 cites Recital C, receipt on August 3, and expiry of the 30-day period on September 2, 2026. It notes this was before the September 21 Amendment and concludes the increase is deemed accepted.

Issue 2 explains that Amendment § 2.1 removes the recall-cost carve-out and limits the indemnity carve-out to § 9.1(c) IP claims. It says recall and product defect/personal injury exposure is now subject to the six-month-fees cap.

The response identifies new § 14.4 and the loss of the consent right. It never says assignment to a competitor is possible, and never notes that Harrowgate remains bound by § 14.3, which makes the restriction one-sided.
The response never mentions Supply Agreement § 15.2 or the rule that written amendments take precedence over the Supply Agreement.
Issue 2 refers to the § 11.1 cap as six months of container fees (the 'six-month-fees cap'), which conveys the cap amount.
The response is a memo addressed to the Partner, with numbered issues. Each issue gives the document and section and a recommended fix.
The response proposes specific language, including a narrowed § 3.1, a restored § 11.2, and a revised § 14.4.
The response concludes the objection window expired and the increase is deemed accepted. It suggests only a possible challenge based on deficient notice.
The response says the integration clause supersedes the term sheet and that the broader § 3.1 governs, so a further amendment is needed.
